key_insight: Data reuploading expands a quantum model’s usable frequency spectrum in a precisely characterizable way, but its expressive growth is polynomial and capacity scales with the number of accessible frequencies.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical rule for designing quantum neural networks: reuploading increases expressivity, yet performance depends strongly on encoding choice, input dimension, and the resulting capacity-cost tradeoff.
method: Derive the accessible Fourier frequencies of an R-reupload quantum circuit as a repeated sumset of the encoding spectrum.
Characterize the spectrum exactly via integer-lattice word length and show its directions stabilize after one reupload while its size grows polynomially.
Use the spectrum size to obtain a Rademacher-complexity capacity bound for quantum data reuploaders.
evidence_signal: Experiments on function approximation and classification, with train/test splits and matched baselines, show the simulated spectra agree with theory and that a single-qubit QDR can outperform an MLP on some low-dimensional or periodic tasks but not on harder multivariate regression.
watch_item: The model is highly sensitive to input-encoding scale and becomes weak relative to classical baselines on higher-dimensional regression, so careful encoding calibration is essential.
paper_title: On the Expressive Power and Capacity of Quantum Data Reuploaders
